title: Atomic structure: nucleus and electron shells
statement: understand that atoms are mostly empty space surrounding a very small, dense nucleus that contains protons and neutrons; electrons are found in shells in the empty space around the nucleus

title: Charges and masses of subatomic particles
statement: identify and describe protons, neutrons and electrons in terms of their relative charges and relative masses

title: Atomic, proton, mass and nucleon number
statement: understand the terms atomic and proton number; mass and nucleon number

title: Distribution of mass and charge in an atom
statement: describe the distribution of mass and charge within an atom

title: Deflection of particle beams in an electric field
statement: describe the behaviour of beams of protons, neutrons and electrons moving at the same velocity in an electric field

title: Counting protons, neutrons and electrons
statement: determine the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons present in both atoms and ions given atomic or proton number, mass or nucleon number and charge

title: Trends in atomic and ionic radius
statement: state and explain qualitatively the variations in atomic radius and ionic radius across a period and down a group

title: Definition of isotope
statement: define the term isotope in terms of numbers of protons and neutrons

title: Isotope nuclide notation
statement: understand the notation $^{A}_{Z}X$ for isotopes, where $A$ is the mass or nucleon number and $Z$ is the atomic or proton number

title: Isotopes and chemical properties
statement: state that and explain why isotopes of the same element have the same chemical properties

title: Isotopes and physical properties
statement: state that and explain why isotopes of the same element have different physical properties, limited to mass and density

title: Shells, sub-shells, orbitals and quantum number
statement: understand the terms: (a) shells, sub-shells and orbitals (b) principal quantum number ($n$) (c) ground state, limited to electronic configuration

title: Orbitals and electron capacity of s, p, d
statement: describe the number of orbitals making up s, p and d sub-shells, and the number of electrons that can fill s, p and d sub-shells

title: Energy order of sub-shells
statement: describe the order of increasing energy of the sub-shells within the first three shells and the 4s and 4p sub-shells

title: Writing electronic configurations
statement: describe the electronic configurations to include the number of electrons in each shell, sub-shell and orbital

title: Electron configuration and inter-electron repulsion
statement: explain the electronic configurations in terms of energy of the electrons and inter-electron repulsion

title: Deducing electronic configuration of atoms and ions
statement: determine the electronic configuration of atoms and ions given the atomic or proton number and charge, using either of the following conventions: e.g. for Fe: $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^6 4s^2$ (full electronic configuration) or $\ce{[Ar]}\,3d^6 4s^2$ (shorthand electronic configuration)

title: Electrons-in-boxes notation
statement: understand and use the electrons in boxes notation, e.g. for Fe: $\ce{[Ar]}$ 3d and 4s sub-shells shown as boxes with arrows representing paired and unpaired electrons

title: Shapes of s and p orbitals
statement: describe and sketch the shapes of s and p orbitals

title: Definition of a free radical
statement: describe a free radical as a species with one or more unpaired electrons

title: Definition of first ionisation energy
statement: define and use the term first ionisation energy, $IE_1$

title: Equations for successive ionisation energies
statement: construct equations to represent first, second and subsequent ionisation energies

title: Trends in ionisation energy across period and group
statement: identify and explain the trends in ionisation energies across a period and down a group of the Periodic Table

title: Successive ionisation energies of an element
statement: identify and explain the variation in successive ionisation energies of an element

title: Ionisation energy and nuclear attraction
statement: understand that ionisation energies are due to the attraction between the nucleus and the outer electron

title: Factors affecting ionisation energy
statement: explain the factors influencing the ionisation energies of elements in terms of nuclear charge, atomic/ionic radius, shielding by inner shells and sub-shells and spin-pair repulsion

title: Deducing electron configuration from ionisation data
statement: deduce the electronic configurations of elements using successive ionisation energy data

title: Deducing periodic table position from ionisation data
statement: deduce the position of an element in the Periodic Table using successive ionisation energy data

title: Definition of the unified atomic mass unit
statement: define the unified atomic mass unit as one twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom

title: Relative atomic, isotopic, molecular and formula mass
statement: define relative atomic mass, $A_r$, relative isotopic mass, relative molecular mass, $M_r$, and relative formula mass in terms of the unified atomic mass unit
